summary: Intermittent p95/p99 tail spikes and 504s traced to idle-merge + KV-prefetch interaction in continuous batcher
description: Issue summary: BrightMetrics reported intermittent increases in p95/p99 latency and occasional 504 timeouts for chat-generation routes during steady low-to-moderate QPS. Impact: customer-facing latency regressions causing user-facing timeouts and one support SLA breach. Environment: Hosted production cluster serving enterprise customer in us-east on dedicated capacity. Initial observation window: 2026-03-09 22:00 -> 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC.
impact: User-facing slowdowns and periodic 504s on chat endpoints for BrightMetrics (enterprise). Affects ~3% of requests in observed window with p99 > 2.5s and intermittent 504s. Business impact: disruption to live analytics demos and automated alerting from customer side.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightMetrics account on prod-us-east with model vicuna-13b-v1.3 and conversation-style payloads (short prompts, average 60 tokens).
2) Send steady low QPS (1-3 rps) traffic from a few persistent connections to mimic customer pattern (many long-lived streams).
3) Observe p95/p99 latency over 1-2 hours; note intermittent spikes and occasional 504s correlated to batcher flush periods.
4) Collect trace ids from affected requests and compare batcher flush timestamps and KV-prefetch logs.
logs: Sample trace snippets: trace=tr-0a1b2c3d flush_delay_ms=480 linger_timer_ms=1200 kv_prefetch_start=11:23:45.112 kv_prefetch_done=11:23:45.933 worker_wait=820ms -> 504. Error samples attached in S3: s3://redwood-support/sup-23501/traces/ (internal). Also see router logs showing request routed to fallback model variant at 11:23:46.33.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported p99 spikes starting after a config tweak on 2026-03-09. Provided initial graphs and asked for SRE investigation. Assigned to Marco.
2026-03-10 - Marco Liu (SRE): Confirmed p99 spikes in metrics. Noted increased linger_timer variance and periodic worker stalls. Requested request traces and batcher debug logs from staging replica.
2026-03-11 - BrightMetrics (Customer): Sent timeline of their demo runs; observed timeouts clustered around 11:20-11:40 UTC. Mentioned they did not change client behaviour.

2026-03-11 - Marco Liu: Dug into continuous-batcher metrics; observed pattern: when persistent connections had low-per-connection QPS, idle-merge heuristic was inflating coalescing window. KV-prefetch was started early but prefetch result sometimes delayed due to slight GC pauses on host, tying up worker and delaying flush. Hypothesis posted to #support and #sre: idle-merge + early KV-prefetch increases head-of-line wait for short requests.

2026-03-12 - Eng (Runtime): Reproduced locally by toggling batcher idlemode and enabling artificial 200-400ms prefetch delay. Observed p99 spikes and 504s. Created PR with conservative change to idle-merge backoff. Marked as candidate hotfix.

2026-03-13 - Marco Liu: Rolled temporary mitigation (disabled idle-merge on the affected pod group) for BrightMetrics' dedicated fleet; immediate p99 improvement observed. Customer validated reduction in timeouts. Planning full patch rollout next week.
2026-03-13 - Aisha Patel: Communicated mitigation and workaround to customer; set follow-up for permanent fix and monitoring.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The continuous-batcher's idle-merge heuristic increases coalescing linger in low-QPS persistent connections. Combined with eager KV-prefetch, this can create head-of-line waiting where the batch waits for prefetch completion on one request before flushing others.

Evidence: Trace tr-0a1b2c3d shows linger_timer jumped from nominal 50ms to 1200ms during observed spike; corresponding kv_prefetch took ~820ms when worker experienced brief GC pause. Batcher metrics show coincident increase in queued_requests and a dramatic drop in flush_rate for 10s windows.

Repro: Local reproduction achieved by simulating 2 persistent connections with 1rps each and injecting 200-500ms delay in KV-prefetch path. Without idle-merge disabled, p99 replicates. With idle-merge disabled or prefetch made non-blocking, latency stabilizes.

Related artifacts: Log slices in s3 and Grafana dashboard panels (batcher/linger, kv-prefetch latency, worker-gc). Slack thread: #support thread ts 16432. Related internal ticket INT-412 scheduled to track runtime refactor.

Risk assessment: Hotfix (disable idle-merge) reduces batching efficiency and may slightly increase token-level cost but has low roll risk. Permanent fix requires kernel-level change to make KV-prefetch non-blocking / speculative or to ensure batch flush doesn't wait on single-request prefetch.

Next steps: 1) Roll targeted disable across customer's pod group (done). 2) Prepare runtime patch to backoff idle-merge when prefetch is outstanding (PR opened). 3) Add unit/regression tests and synthetic workload in perf lab. 4) Postmortem and follow-up INT ticket to track feature work.
resolution: Mitigation applied: idle-merge heuristic disabled for BrightMetrics pod group on 2026-03-13 14:12 UTC. Observed p99 drop from ~2.8s -> 0.45s and 504 count reduced to 0. Customer confirmed immediate improvement. Permanent fix: runtime PR created to make KV-prefetch non-blocking and to add a conservative cap to idle-merge (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8341). Rollout plan: staged deploy to dedicated clusters with monitoring alarms enabled; target complete by 2026-03-20. Follow-up: INT-412 assigned for refactor and perf validation.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 - Marco Liu: Hotfix deployed to customer's fleet at 14:12 UTC. Metrics show sustained improvement across 12h window.
2026-03-13 - Eng: PR 8341 includes unit tests and a synthetic workload reproducer. Perf impact estimated +1.8% unit token cost in worst case for low-QPS patterns; plan to optimize further.
2026-03-14 - Customer success: Scheduled check-in with BrightMetrics for 2026-03-18 to validate longer-term behaviour and cost implications.
Follow-up action: Create KB article describing workaround (disable idle-merge) and guidance for customers with many long-lived low-QPS connections.
